text: Purpose: Define the minimum document set and core fields required for a patient case review.
Required documents: Every case must contain: (1) Patient Registration Form, (2) Attending Physician Note, (3) Discharge Summary, and (4) Claim Submission Form.
Required claim fields: The Claim Submission Form must include patient identity, admission date, discharge date, primary diagnosis, attending physician, and physician signature.

Procedure-specific support: If the claim includes a procedure listed in SOP-05, the corresponding supporting report is also required. Review action A missing required core document, required claim field, or required procedure-support document must be flagged for review. Do not infer missing content from another document.
Purpose: Ensure all documents belong to the same patient.
Exact identifiers: Patient ID and date of birth must match across the case documents.
Names: Names may be normalized for case, spacing, punctuation, and common title differences. A name difference alone should not automatically be treated as a mismatch if Patient ID and DOB agree.
Escalation: Any Patient ID or DOB mismatch is a high-severity issue and requires human review.
Purpose: Guide comparison of diagnoses across physician notes, discharge summaries, and claim forms.

Semantic equivalence: Equivalent terminology and standard abbreviations should not be flagged as conflicts. Example: “Type 2 diabetes mellitus without complications” and “T2DM, uncomplicated” are equivalent for this review.

True conflict: Different clinical conditions should be flagged when the claim diagnosis contradicts the final documented diagnosis. Example: “Pneumonia” and “Acute bronchitis” are not treated as equivalent.

Uncertainty: A suspected, possible, rule-out, or not-confirmed diagnosis must not be treated as a confirmed diagnosis. If a claim asserts a confirmed diagnosis while the clinical record remains uncertain, escalate for human review. AI behavior The assistant should cite the documents used to make the comparison and should not silently rewrite diagnoses.

policy_title: SOP-04 Admission, Discharge & Procedure Date Validation
text: Purpose: Validate basic chronological consistency.

policy_title: SOP-04 Admission, Discharge & Procedure Date Validation
text: Admission/discharge rule: Discharge date must be the same as or later than the admission date.

policy_title: SOP-04 Admission, Discharge & Procedure Date Validation
text: Procedure date rule: Any procedure date must fall within the documented admission-to-discharge period unless a supporting note explicitly explains otherwise.

policy_title: SOP-04 Admission, Discharge & Procedure Date Validation
text: Severity: A discharge date before admission is a high-severity issue and requires review.
Purpose: Define required evidence for selected procedures.
Colonoscopy: Requires an Endoscopy Report documenting procedure date, findings, and conclusion/impression.
CT abdomen with contrast: Requires a Radiology Report containing at least Study Date, Findings, and Impression.

Appendectomy: Requires an Operative Report containing procedure date, operative findings, and surgeon identification. Missing report If a required procedure report is absent, flag as high severity. Incomplete report If a required report exists but a required section is blank or clearly incomplete, flag for human review. Do not invent the missing section.

policy_title: SOP-06 Human Review Escalation & AI Limits
text: Purpose: Define when the AI assistant must defer to a human reviewer.

policy_title: SOP-06 Human Review Escalation & AI Limits
text: Mandatory escalation: Escalate when there is conflicting clinical evidence, uncertain diagnosis status, incomplete supporting evidence, identity mismatch, or a rule outcome cannot be determined confidently.

policy_title: SOP-06 Human Review Escalation & AI Limits
text: Decision boundary: The AI assistant may identify issues and summarize evidence. It must not autonomously approve, reject, or deny a claim.

policy_title: SOP-06 Human Review Escalation & AI Limits
text: Uncertainty: When evidence is insufficient, the correct output is “needs_review” with a clear reason, not a guessed conclusion.
Purpose: Ensure every AI-generated issue can be traced back to source documents.
Evidence requirement: Every reported issue must identify the source document and the relevant field, section, or quoted value used as evidence.
No unsupported claims: The assistant must distinguish documented facts from hypotheses and must not fabricate missing values.
Audit trail: A production design should preserve case ID, input document references, rule or model version, output, and review outcome for later audit.
